thread.title: UPDATE: Chinese stocks end at 2-year low, Apple suppliers sink on trade-war worries

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Chinese stocks end at 2-year low, Apple suppliers sink on trade-war worries
text:
By Dow Jones Newswire
iPhone component-makers' shares hit hard in Hong Kong, Taiwan
Asian exporters took a heavy hit Tuesday, with China stocks suffering their lowest close in two years, following President Donald Trump's announcement of potentially $400 billion in additional tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-seeks-additional-200-billion-in-tariffs-against-china-and-threatens-even-more-2018-06-18)against imports from that country.
In Japan, the yen jumped on that news, leaving the Nikkei to finish down 1.8%. Export-related stocks slid, with Komatsu (6301.TO) shedding 2.5% while Honda (HMC) slumped 1.6%. The dollar was down 0.7% versus the yen at Yen109.77.
China stocks closed at their worst levels since June 2016 following Monday's holiday and amid increased trade tensions with the U.S. The Shanghai Composite fell 3.8% to and the Shenzhen Composite slid 6% to 1,666.66, its worst finish since September 2015.
ZTE Corp. (000063.SZ) slid 25% on Tuesday after the U.S. Senate late Monday passed legislation to reinstate a ban on the selling of U.S. components to the Chinese telecommunications company. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/senate-rejects-trump-deal-reinstates-ban-against-zte-2018-06-18)
Opinion:Fight over trade policy is like the fight over vaccines: there's a lot of wrong information (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fight-over-trade-policy-is-like-the-fight-over-vaccines-theres-a-lot-of-wrong-information-2018-06-12)
Meanwhile, Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi Corp. has decided to put off a widely anticipated initial public offering in mainland China, without giving a reason (https://www.wsj.com/articles/xiaomi-shelves-china-share-sale-as-regulators-iron-out-new-rules-1529387852).
Apple Inc. (AAPL) suppliers' stocks were hit hard around the region, despite a report that U.S. tariffs would spare iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-reportedly-told-apple-that-tariffs-against-china-would-spare-iphones-2018-06-18) produced in China.
IPhone-camera maker Cowell E Holdings (1415.HK) slumped 12% in Hong Kong to fresh record lows, while smartphone-lens maker Sunny Optical (2382.HK) pulled back 5.3% and acoustics firm AAC Technologies (2018.HK) dropped 3.3%. In Taiwan, Sunny peer Largan Precision (3008.TW) ended down 5.2%. Apple product assembler Hon Hai Precision Industry (2317.TW) dropped 2.4%.
The Hong Kong Hang Seng Index closed down 2.8%, led by a 5.7% drop for Hong Kong-listed Chinese pork producer WH Group , which owns U.S.'s Smithfield Foods and is vulnerable to potential pork and soybean tariffs. Taiwan's TAIEX slid 1.7%.
Meanwhile, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 finished flat, as the Aussie dollar eased on global trade tensions. Korea's benchmark dropped 1.5% and New Zealand's NZX fell 1.2%.
From Tokyo, came one bright spot for otherwise battered Asian markets, with flea-market app Mercari Inc. (4385.TO) , closing up 77% over the offering price in To (https://www.wsj.com/articles/flea-market-app-mercari-soars-in-tokyo-debut-1529389761)kyo, bringing its valuation to around $6.5 billion.
-- Saumya Vaishampayan contributed to this report
-Dow Jones Newswire; 19-18 0550ET
